bear: Prices for everyday things rose 3.7% from a year ago, which is higher than people want
Oil jumped over 10% in one week, which makes gas and shipping more expensive
Some AI companies have borrowed huge amounts of money, and investors worry they can't pay it back
Higher interest rates make safer choices like savings and bonds more attractive than stocks
bull: The market is only about 2% below its all-time high
Investors think the Federal Reserve probably won't raise interest rates in October
Big companies like Goldman Sachs and TSMC made more money than expected
Stocks bounced back on Oct 19 as investors bought shares that had dropped
briefs.headline: The market slipped from its record high this month
briefs.name: S&P 500
briefs.nextEvent: The Federal Reserve meets October 27-28 to decide on interest rates, and Microsoft, Amazon and Apple share their results

sources.title: Stock market outlook for the week of 19-23 October 2026

briefs.summary: The S&P 500 is a group of 500 of the biggest US companies, so it shows how the whole market is doing. It fell about 2% in the week ending Oct 16, to 7,659. Prices rising faster than expected, oil going over $100 a barrel, and worries about companies borrowing a lot of money for AI all made investors nervous.

bear: The Nasdaq broke the steady upward trend it had been on since April
Investors are asking whether all the money spent on AI will actually pay off
Chip stocks fell around the world, and South Korea's market dropped so fast that trading was paused
High oil prices, rising prices for everyday things, and higher interest rates hurt tech stocks the most
bull: After the big drop, many tech stocks were cheaper, and buyers jumped in quickly
Citigroup thinks AI could drive almost 70% of company profit growth around the world next year
Companies keep signing big AI deals, like reported talks to sell about $45 billion of computing power to Anthropic
The selling seems to be slowing down
briefs.headline: Tech stocks had their worst week since June, then bounced a little
briefs.name: Nasdaq
briefs.nextEvent: Big tech companies report their results over the next two weeks, starting with Microsoft on October 27

sources.title: Chart of the day: US100 (Nasdaq 100) rebound in AI trade vs weakening technical picture

briefs.summary: The Nasdaq is full of tech companies, so it shows how tech stocks are doing. It fell 4.5% in the week ending Oct 16, mostly because computer chip stocks dropped hard. It went back up 1.1% on Oct 19, but experts said that was a small bounce, not a full recovery.

bear: Apple expects sales to grow 9% to 11% next quarter, less than the 12% experts hoped for
Some of last quarter's profit came from a one-time refund on tariffs (taxes on imports), so it won't happen again
The stock is already expensive, so a lot of good news is already in the price
A few experts think the stock is worth less, between $250 and $304
bull: Sales grew 16% to $109.4 billion, and profit per share beat what experts expected
iPhone sales grew about 22%, and services like the App Store and iCloud grew 12%
Several big banks raised their price goals, some as high as $380 to $400
New AI-powered devices, including a foldable iPhone, could get people to upgrade
briefs.headline: Apple had a great quarter, but experts disagree on how much higher it can go
briefs.nextEvent: Apple shares its next results on November 2, 2026

sources.title: Apple stock forecast: Wall Street analysts split on AAPL's upside

briefs.summary: Apple made more money than expected last quarter thanks to strong iPhone sales, and its stock is near its highest price of the year at about $343 (Oct 16). Most experts still say buy, but their average price goal is now a little below today's price. Apple also predicted slower growth than people hoped, and the stock is expensive: buyers are paying about 39 times Apple's yearly profit per share.

bear: Over the last year, Amazon spent $7.6 billion more cash than it brought in, after bringing in $18.2 billion extra the year before
It spent $66.1 billion more on buildings and equipment, mostly for AI
Some investors wonder if spending this much on AI can last, which caused a drop the week before
bull: AWS sales grew 37% to $42.2 billion last quarter
Total sales grew 20% to $200.6 billion, and profit from operations rose to $27.5 billion from $19.2 billion
Morgan Stanley, a big bank, changed its view on the stock and AI stocks bounced back
briefs.headline: Amazon's cloud business is booming, but it's spending a ton on AI
briefs.nextEvent: Amazon shares its next results on October 29, 2026

sources.title: Amazon Stock News (Oct 20, 2026): AMZN Rises 5.0% to $262.45

briefs.summary: Amazon's stock jumped 5% to $262.45 on Oct 19 after a big bank changed its view on the stock and AI stocks bounced back. Amazon Web Services (AWS), which rents computing power to other companies, is growing 37% a year. The catch: Amazon is spending so much on AI data centers that it spent more cash than it brought in over the last year.

bear: Profit missed expectations even without the one-time investment loss
Money from bond trading fell 4%, and fees from helping companies raise money dropped 8% from last quarter
Costs went up 12%, and it set aside $2.7 billion for loans that might not get paid back
Experts may lower their price goals after the miss
bull: Sales rose 8% to $50.2 billion, and the amount it lent out grew 10%
It keeps a big cushion of money set aside for safety, and it earns a strong return for its owners
The bank expects the money it earns from loans to grow about 10% next year
The stock is fairly priced compared with its profits, and some banks think it can reach $400 to $420
briefs.headline: JPMorgan missed expectations for the first time since 2023, but it's still very profitable
briefs.nextEvent: JPMorgan shares its next results in mid-January 2027

sources.title: JPMorgan Chase stock forecast after earnings miss

briefs.summary: JPMorgan, the biggest bank in the US, earned $5.57 per share last quarter, below the $5.85 experts expected. Part of that was a $658 million loss on investments. Shares were around $336 on Oct 13. Its loans and everyday banking keep growing, but some parts of the business slowed down and costs went up.

bear: Microsoft plans to spend about $175 billion on data centers in 2026, which could shrink its profit margins
All that spending has already cut the extra cash it brings in
If Azure grows less than about 45%, investors will be disappointed, and the stock has jumped or dropped up to 15% after recent results
bull: Microsoft says customer demand is bigger than what it can supply
Cloud sales passed $214 billion last year, almost two-thirds of all its sales
Sales of Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, Teams) should grow faster as it starts charging for AI features
briefs.headline: Microsoft's results on Oct 27 will show if its cloud business is still growing fast
briefs.nextEvent: Microsoft shares its next results on October 27, 2026

sources.title: Which Dates Could Move Microsoft Stock Most?

briefs.summary: Microsoft's stock is up about 34% over three months because companies want its cloud and AI services. Microsoft says customers want more than it can provide right now. Its next results are the big test: investors expect its cloud service, Azure, to grow about 45%. The worry is how much Microsoft is spending on data centers.

bear: Nvidia isn't counting on any data center sales in China
Interest rates on government bonds rose to about 5.1%, which usually hurts expensive tech stocks
Worries about how customers will pay for AI caused a big drop in chip stocks in mid-October
bull: Sales were $96.2 billion last quarter, up 106% from a year ago
It keeps about 75 cents of every dollar in sales after the cost of making its chips, which is very high
Its new Vera Rubin chips are going into full production, and the CEO says demand is speeding up
briefs.headline: Nvidia is still growing fast, but AI stocks got shaky this month
briefs.nextEvent: Nvidia's biggest customers (Meta, Microsoft, Amazon) share their results over the next two weeks, and their AI spending plans move Nvidia's stock

sources.title: Nvidia Stock News (Oct 20, 2026): NVDA Rises 1.4% to $217.09

briefs.summary: Nvidia makes the chips that power AI. Its sales more than doubled last quarter, and its CEO says demand is speeding up as its new Vera Rubin chips start shipping. The stock bounced to about $217 on Oct 19 after a week of AI chip stocks falling, leaving it about 11% below its high for the year. The worries are about how AI companies will pay for all their spending, rising interest rates, and China.

bear: Profit from running the business fell 56% to $718 million
Spending on research grew 69% as Tesla puts more money into AI and robots
Sales from its energy business, like home and grid batteries, fell 16% and missed expectations
Money from selling emission credits to other carmakers fell 73%, so that easy profit is fading
bull: Tesla delivered 486,532 cars, over 24,000 more than experts expected
It kept 19.6% of each sales dollar after costs, up from 16.8% last quarter
It brought in $1.53 billion more cash than it spent, after spending $1.09 billion more than it brought in the quarter before
Paid Full Self-Driving subscriptions grew 67% to 1.74 million
briefs.headline: Tesla beat expectations, but its operating profit fell by more than half
briefs.nextEvent: Tesla shares how many cars it delivered in early January
briefs.summary: Tesla shared its results on Oct 21. Sales stayed flat at $28.05 billion, and profit per share of $0.48 beat the $0.45 experts expected. It kept more money on each car it sold and brought in more cash than it spent. But spending on AI, self-driving taxis and its Optimus robot cut its operating profit by 56%.
